key_insight: Among the tested HVOF cermet coatings, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall balance of dense microstructure, highest hardness, and lowest friction, making it the top performer.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical machine and power-engineering parts, coating composition and binder selection strongly control durability, adhesion, and tribological performance.
method: HVOF-sprayed WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr coatings onto 65G steel.
Characterized microstructure by SEM/EDS and measured microhardness, roughness, friction, and adhesive strength.
Compared performance across coatings to identify the most wear-resistant formulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports measured outcomes including friction coefficients, microhardness values, surface roughness, and scratch/adhesion behavior, with WC–Co–Cr showing μ = 0.143 and 1316.87 HV.
watch_item: Performance depends on spraying conditions and adhesion can drop for some compositions, so process control is critical before scale-up.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
